info.title: PersonalFi API
info.description: Self-hosted personal finance and advisory. Single user, zero public ingress. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details; clients switch on `code`, never on `detail`.

type.description: Stable URI identifying the problem kind.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary. Does not change per occurrence.

code.description: Stable machine code the client switches on.

correlationId.description: Quote this when reporting the failure.

minor.description: Minor units as a decimal string. Never a JSON number.

MoneyInput.description: An amount of money. Negative is an outflow.

id.description: This row. Changes on every sync; not a security id.

name.description: The provider's own name for the security.

ticker.description: The provider's own ticker, as given.

institutionValue.description: The institution's own value for the position, as reported. Not a price × quantity.

reasons.description: Why it could not be identified, in plain words, one sentence each.

close.description: A decimal string. Never a JSON number (D3).

priceDate.description: The observation used — not necessarily the date asked for.

gain.description: `null` whenever the status is unavailable. Never a zero standing in for unknown.

weight.description: Share of the valued portfolio, as a Ratio string.

closingValue.description: Σ priced positions on `to`: the value at `to`.

netContributions.description: Σ external flows in (from, to], positive = net money in: contributions, withdrawals, transfers in and out (in kind, valued at the transfer date). The same flows the TWR and MWR are measured against.

dividendsAndInterest.description: Cash dividends, fund distributions and interest.

reinvestedDividends.description: Reinvested dividends, apart: a broker reporting both legs would otherwise count one twice.

feesPaid.description: Fee rows plus commissions on trades. A magnitude.

taxesWithheld.description: Taxes withheld in the account. A magnitude.

complete.description: false when anything below was excluded.

unresolvedSecurities.description: Positions the resolver could not identify (WP 10.4): outside every valuation, named.

unresolvedMovements.description: Movements in a security nobody could identify (WP 10.4): listed in Activity, left out of every flow — their value is outside the valuation too, so counting the flow alone would book the money as a loss.

accountIds.description: The accounts measured; empty for the whole portfolio (every account).

current.description: Contribution to net worth. A card you owe on is negative.

limit.description: A magnitude, not a contribution: always positive.

effective.description: null: the account has no tax bucket.

source.description: `provider_subtype`: the provider’s own subtype named it. `provider_fallback`: nothing recognised the subtype and TAXABLE is assumed — a guess, not a fact.

override.description: What the holder set, if anything.

management.description: Who manages the account (WP 10.3): advisor, robo_advisor or self_directed. `null` is unclassified — the holder has not said, and nothing infers it. Groups `GET /investments/performance/by-management`; moves no projection.

mask.description: Last 2-4 digits. Never the full number.

balance.description: null until a balance has been observed.

asOf.description: The oldest balance the totals rest on.

NetWorthInput.description: Net worth from the latest balance of every included account, per currency. `inputs` is the audit trail: every account, whether it counted, and why not.

icon.description: A Lucide icon name (decision D20). A key, never markup.

isSystem.description: true for a row the shipped taxonomy installed.

syncJobId.description: The queued backfill, when one was queued.

syncRunId.description: The completed backfill, when it ran inline.

mode.description: `inline` means the adapter stages in this process and could not be queued.

deduped.description: A sync of this connection was already queued or running.

maxSeq.description: Highest event sequence, as a string: it is a bigint.

maxLagEvents.description: Events the furthest-behind consumer has not read.

failedConsumers.description: Consumers stopped at an event they cannot handle.

stalled.description: Running jobs whose worker stopped heartbeating.

type.description: The house vocabulary the lot engine reads (`BUY`, `CASH`, …).

name.description: The provider’s description of the movement.

security.description: null: the movement is about no security (cash, a fee, a deposit), or about one nobody could identify — then `unresolvedSecurity` is set.

quantity.description: Signed as the provider reported it: negative on a disposal.

price.description: Unit price; null when nobody stated one.

amount.description: House sign: negative = cash left the account.

flow.description: For a contribution or withdrawal: the external flow the performance route measures against, positive = into the portfolio. A 401(k) payroll contribution arrives as a buy whose `amount` is the cash the buy spent; `flow` is the money that arrived. null for everything else, and for an in-kind transfer (valued only by the performance route, at the transfer date).

activitySync.description: `synced`: the investment-activity leg has completed at least once. `pending`: it has not run yet (an empty list is not "no activity"). `failed`: it ran and never completed. `not_applicable`: activity for this account arrives by import or by hand.

purpose.description: What the key is for, one line, from the RUNBOOK.

source.description: `file`: the operator's secret file supplies the key (it wins; read-only here). `stored`: this holder's key, sealed in the install. `none`: neither.

configured.description: True when a key is in force (file or stored).

anonymous.description: OpenFIGI only: no key, and the anonymous tier is in use (10 jobs per request).

keyHint.description: The last four characters of the stored key. Never the key.

storedAt.description: When the stored key was first saved.

rotatedAt.description: When the stored key was last replaced.

narrowedOut.description: True when MARKET_DATA_ALLOWED_HOSTS excludes this provider's host.

asOfDate.description: The holder’s calendar day the refresh priced as of.

priceable.description: Held securities whose kind a provider prices (`priced + unpriced`).

notPricedByProvider.description: Cash, bonds and other kinds no provider prices. Not asked about.

reason.description: `source_not_configured`: no key for the provider that prices this kind (by file or in Settings), or MARKET_DATA_ALLOWED_HOSTS excludes it; no request was made. `no_ticker` / `no_coin_id`: the planner could not build what the provider prices by. `no_data`: the provider answered with no close. `skipped_no_key`, `rate_limited`, `refused`, `error`: as the adapter reported them. `no_provider_for_kind`: no provider prices this kind.

anyOf.description: `source_not_configured`: no key for the provider that prices this kind (by file or in Settings), or MARKET_DATA_ALLOWED_HOSTS excludes it; no request was made. `no_ticker` / `no_coin_id`: the planner could not build what the provider prices by. `no_data`: the provider answered with no close. `skipped_no_key`, `rate_limited`, `refused`, `error`: as the adapter reported them. `no_provider_for_kind`: no provider prices this kind.

Every account, with its latest balance
get.description: Closed accounts are hidden by default. They keep every transaction they ever had — "delete the account" and "stop showing me this account" are different requests.

patch.summary: Include an account in net worth, or close it
patch.description: The two fields a user owns. An account name comes from the provider and is not editable in Phase 1 — there is no nickname column yet (see the WP 1.5 evidence note).

put.summary: Set what an account is: its tax treatment, role, valuation basis and who manages it
put.description: The holder’s overlay on the provider’s facts, which are never mutated. A **full replacement**: an omitted or `null` field is cleared, and when none is left the override is removed. `taxTreatment` outranks the provider-subtype default the projection starts from (CF-16). `valuation: "balance"` counts an investment or crypto account that has no priced holdings at its latest balance instead of leaving it out — labelled as such wherever it appears (O-2). `management` (advisor, robo_advisor, self_directed) groups the performance-by-management comparison and moves no projection. Changing tax treatment, role or valuation makes a stored projection read `stale`, naming the change; nothing is recomputed. Another holder’s account is a 404, exactly as a missing one. Emits `ledger.AccountOverrideChanged`. Session only: no money moves.

delete.summary: Clear every override on an account, back to the provider’s defaults
delete.description: Idempotent: clearing an account with no override changes nothing. A stored projection computed with the override reads `stale` afterwards, as for any change. Another holder’s account is a 404. Session only: no money moves.

get.summary: Which accounts net worth leaves out, and which it counts by the holder’s say-so
get.description: Computed live by the same valuation the net-worth snapshot uses, without FX and without writing. `unvalued` is every account in net worth that cannot be valued — an investment account with no priced holdings, an account with no balance — and is never counted as zero. `byBalance` is every account counted at its latest balance because the holder set `valuation: "balance"`. The plan and net-worth screens name both, so a figure is never quietly missing an account (O-2).

get.summary: Net worth now, per currency
get.description: Totals are reported per currency and never summed across them: there is no FX table in Phase 1, and adding dollars to euros would be a wrong number rendered confidently.

post.summary: Record a balance for a manual account
post.description: Only for `provider: "manual"` accounts (see this file's module comment) — a 422 otherwise. Appends through `recordBalance`, the same writer a sync uses, with `source: "manual"`; it never replaces a prior observation, so a correction is a new row with a later `asOf`, not an edit of an old one. Needs a step-up assertion, the same policy `connections.ts` uses for every write that moves net worth.

limit.description: A magnitude, not a contribution: always positive.

asOf.description: Defaults to now — when the observation is entered, not backdated.

post.summary: Add one or more hand-entered transactions to a manual account
post.description: Only for `provider: "manual"` accounts — a 422 otherwise. Builds each row through `@connector/manual`'s `manualTransaction()`, which computes the mandatory fingerprint (08 §2.5) and a content-hash id, so entering the same row twice is one row and a later real import of the same charge reconciles against it rather than duplicating it. Writes through `applyProviderTransactions`, the same function every adapter's sync uses, so `categorization.AssignmentsChanged` and budgeting's consumer see a typed transaction exactly like a synced one. Needs a step-up assertion, the same policy `connections.ts` uses for every write that moves net worth.

name.description: What the user typed. Never sniffed.

get.summary: The transaction feed
get.description: Keyset pagination over `(date DESC, id DESC)`. Pass `nextCursor` back verbatim; it is opaque and a client that parses it will break. `summary` is returned on the first page of a filter (no `cursor`) and is `null` on subsequent pages.

get.summary: Every matching transaction, as CSV
get.description: Needs a step-up assertion (decision D21). A stolen session cookie must not be enough to walk out with the complete history. Accepts the same filters as the list.

get.summary: One transaction, with provenance, splits and its transfer link

patch.description: Provider facts are immutable. This writes intent — note, category, exclusion, payee name — which the resolver layers over the fact and which survives every re-sync.

post.summary: Apply one overlay patch to many transactions
post.description: One transaction, so a bulk categorise is one undo entry and one toast (05 §5.3). An id that does not exist fails the whole batch rather than being skipped silently.

post.summary: Divide a transaction across categories
post.description: Replaces the existing splits wholesale. The lines must sum to the transaction, to the cent, in its currency: a set that does not is `ledger.splits_do_not_sum` (422).

post.summary: "Always categorise like this" — a rule seeded from one transaction
post.description: The wp1.4/wp1.6 carry-over ("Rule-from-transaction" — `createRuleFromTransaction` existed in `@ctx/categorization` with no route). Builds a `payee contains <cleaned descriptor>` condition and a `set_category` action from this transaction's own payee, validated exactly as `POST /rules` validates one: `categoryKey` must name a leaf category belonging to this user. `POST /rules/preview` is how to see what a retroactive apply of the new rule would change before running it. A session is enough — see `rules.ts`'s module comment for why this file's rules routes need no step-up assertion.

post.summary: Confirm that two rows are one movement of money
post.description: Confidence 1.0 and `user_confirmed`: this is not a heuristic. Any standing rejection of the same pair is withdrawn, so the next pairing run does not silently refuse to re-propose what the user just confirmed.

post.summary: Say no to a transfer pairing, permanently
post.description: `transactionId` is **either leg** of the pair; the other is read from the link. The rejection is recorded as well as undone, so the heuristic does not re-propose it.

otherTransactionId.description: Required only when the two rows are not currently linked.

get.summary: Every provider this deployment can link
get.description: The "Add a connection" screen, as data. A new adapter appears here by being registered at the composition root; no UI change is required (08 §2.7).

get.summary: Every connection, with status and freshness
get.description: No credential appears in this payload — not as a field, not as a redacted placeholder, not as a boolean called `hasToken`. `status` plus `errorSince` is what the UI actually needs to say "stale for 26 hours".

post.summary: Link a provider
post.description: Needs a step-up assertion (D21). `input` is opaque and validated by the adapter — a Plaid public token, a set of manual accounts, a file upload descriptor. A union here would have to grow with every provider and would be wrong the first time one changed its link flow. Re-linking an institution already connected updates that row and preserves its cursor and accounts; it never creates a second one.

get.summary: One connection, its accounts and its recent runs

delete.description: Needs a step-up assertion (D21). Revokes at the provider best-effort, then destroys the local credential — the local half always happens, because a provider that is down must not be able to stop a user from disconnecting. **Accounts, transactions and the sync history are kept**: "disconnect" and "delete my data" are different requests and only one of them is reversible. `revokedAtProvider: false` means we could not tell the provider; with Plaid the Item still occupies a billing slot until it is removed there, so the UI should say so.

providerSlotMayRemain.description: True when revocation failed: the provider may still hold the item.

post.summary: Finish a link whose flow ran in the browser
post.description: The second half of a provider-hosted flow (08 §3.6): the user came back from Plaid Link with a public token and this exchanges it. Needs a step-up assertion. The resulting connection must be the one named in the path, or this is a 409 — silently creating a second connection under the first one’s URL is how a net worth doubles.

post.summary: Replace the credential on an existing connection
post.description: Needs a step-up assertion: a new credential is an addition, not a read. The cursor and every mapped account survive, which is the whole point — 08 §3.9, "losing account identity on reconnect is the classic way a personal finance app silently doubles a user’s net worth". `reconnectFlow` on the connector says what the UI should have collected: `provider_hosted`, `credential_form`, `reupload` or `none`.

relinked.description: True when this replaced the credential on an existing row.

syncJobId.description: The queued backfill, when one was queued.

syncRunId.description: The completed backfill, when it ran inline.

post.summary: Ask for a sync now
post.description: Returns the queued work, never the result: the result is in `sync_runs` and on the event stream. Deduped and singleton on the connection — a webhook, the nightly schedule and an impatient user cannot start three cursor loops on one connection, which 04 §4.4 calls "the fastest way to corrupt cursor state".

get.summary: The sync history
get.description: 08 §6.3: "`sync_runs` is the observability surface that matters… this single feature eliminates most 'why is my balance wrong' debugging". Every attempt leaves a row, including the ones that failed before the first page.

post.summary: Import a CSV, OFX/QFX or QIF file
post.description: Creates a file-import connection on the first upload and stages onto it thereafter, then runs the import **synchronously** — a file upload has no meaningful "come back later", and the adapter stages in this process (see the module comment). Re-importing the same file changes nothing: every row is identified by a hash of its own content, and the ledger’s natural key catches whatever the staging layer misses.

connectionId.description: Omit to create a new file-import connection.

skipped.description: Rows already staged by an earlier upload.

get.summary: This user's chart of categories, in display order
get.description:
Flat and ordered: a child follows its parent, and `parentId` carries the structure. Archived categories are omitted unless asked for — a picker must not offer a category the user retired, but a historic assignment still points at one. Categories are per user (decision D6), so this is never a shared list.

Taxonomy is seeded once, at user creation, by `bootstrap-seed.ts`'s `seedUserState` (condition C-1, docs/evidence/phase-2/gate-security-review.md §5) — this route used to carry a D2-1 lazy repair for the gap that left; the repair is gone and this route is a plain read.

parameters.name: includeArchived
parameters.description: Default false. Set only by a management screen, never by a picker.

post.summary: Create a custom category
post.description: 05 §5.2's "create new category" escape hatch. `parentId: null` creates a new top-level heading; a non-null `parentId` creates a leaf under it and inherits its `kind` (a leaf cannot have a different kind than its parent — that is what keeps a spend report's totals meaning what they say). The two-level `CHECK` (migration 0006) is enforced before the write: a `parentId` that already has a parent of its own is refused, not silently flattened.

kind.description: Only used when `parentId` is null. A leaf inherits its parent's.

patch.description: Deliberately narrow: `label`, `description` and `icon` only. `kind` and the parent/child structure are not editable here — both are structural (the seeding pass's own rule for why a re-seed never touches them) and changing either after transactions have been filed under a category is how a report silently moves money between totals. Works on a system category as well as a custom one: a user renaming "Dining & Drinks" to "Eating Out" is exactly what this is for.

delete.description: Archives, never deletes (same reasoning as a closed account or a removed transaction): every `category_assignments`, `rules` and provider-mapping row that points at this id keeps resolving exactly as before, and `GET /categories` simply omits it unless `includeArchived` is asked for. Archiving a heading also archives its non-archived children — a leaf left visible under a heading the picker no longer shows would be reachable only by id, which is a worse state than archiving both. Idempotent: archiving an already-archived category is a 200 with `changed: false`.

post.summary: Create a rule
post.description: Validated the same way a stored rule is re-validated on read (`rules/schema.ts`): a `set_category` action must name a leaf category that belongs to this user — a custom category (`POST /categories`) or a system one, never another user's.

patch.description: Partial: an omitted field keeps its stored value.

delete.description: A hard delete — `rule_runs` cascades with it (migration 0006). Unlike a category, a rule carries no history another row points back at, so there is nothing an archive would preserve.

post.summary: Preview what applying a rule retroactively would change
post.description: Writes nothing, emits no event: "this will change 912 transactions" shown before the fact is what turns a retroactive apply from a trap into a tool. Runs the exact code path `POST /rules/{id}/apply` runs, so the count it shows is the count that will actually happen.

retroactive.description: Without this, only transactions with no user category are matched.

post.summary: Apply a rule retroactively
post.description: The non-preview half of `POST /rules/preview` — see this file's module comment for why it exists here. Emits `categorization.RuleApplied`.

post.summary: A Plaid Link token for a new connection
post.description: Step one of a provider-hosted link (08 §3.6): the pins are `PlaidConnector`'s own (products transactions+investments+liabilities, 730 days, PFC v2, the configured redirect_uri) — see wp1.3-plaid.md §1. Read-only: nothing in this application changes as a result of calling it.

post.summary: Finish a Plaid Link flow and create the connection
post.description: Needs a step-up assertion (D21) — this is the moment a real credential is stored, exactly like `POST /connections`. Exchanges the public token, creates (or re-links) the connection, and schedules the first sync through the orchestrator. Refuses an eleventh Plaid connection (D16: Trial's 10-Item cap; `/item/remove` does not free a slot, so this counts every Plaid row ever created, including a disconnected one).

institutionName.description: From Link's own metadata; falls back to /item/get when omitted.

post.summary: A Plaid Link token in update mode, for reconnect
post.description: Needs a step-up assertion: it opens the connection's sealed credential to build the request. 01 §1.7: "the access_token does not change when using Link in update mode" — no `products` on the wire (a `products` array in update mode re-initialises the Item's product set and can re-bill it — wp1.3-plaid.md §1), and nothing here needs re-sealing. Completing the reauth still goes through the existing `POST /connections/{id}/reconnect`.

accountSelectionEnabled.description: 01 §1.7: any de-selected account stops being shared. Off by default so a routine reauth cannot silently drop an account.

get.summary: Where Plaid is configured from, without the secret
get.description: Whether Plaid is usable, and whether that is the operator's secret files (read-only), this holder’s stored credentials, or neither. Carries the environment and the last four characters of the stored client id. The secret is never returned.

put.summary: Store (or replace) this holder’s Plaid credentials
put.description: Needs a step-up assertion (D21). Checks the credentials against Plaid (a Link token request: authenticated, free) before sealing them under the KEK. Refused with 409 when the operator's secret files configure Plaid, 403 for `production` without PLAID_ALLOW_PRODUCTION, 422 when Plaid rejects the credentials, 502 when Plaid cannot be reached. The response is the same shape as the GET; the secret is never returned.

secret.description: Plaid secret for the chosen environment. Never echoed back.

delete.summary: Remove this holder’s stored Plaid credentials
delete.description: Needs a step-up assertion (D21). Deletes the sealed row and retires its key. Revokes nothing at Plaid: the key stays valid there until rolled in the Plaid dashboard, and connections linked with it stop syncing. Idempotent. Returns the GET shape.

get.summary: Server-sent events for every connection
get.description: `text/event-stream`. Events: `connection.created`, `connection.status`, `sync.progress`, `sync.completed`, `account.upserted`, `balance.recorded`. A `:` comment every 15 seconds keeps a proxy from reaping an idle stream. `id:` is the outbox sequence; send it back as `Last-Event-ID` (or `?from=`) to resume.

get.summary: Server-sent events for one connection
get.description: The link-flow stream: opened after `POST /connections` so the UI can follow the backfill. Carries the three events whose aggregate is a connection — `connection.created`, `connection.status`, `sync.completed`. Per-row progress is aggregated on an account and is on `/sync/stream`.

get.summary: Spending by category and month
get.description: Transfers excluded and refunds netted against their original (`@ctx/budgeting`'s rule, reused unmodified). One cell per `(month, category)`; `categoryId: null` is the uncategorised envelope, present only for a month it was net negative.

get.summary: Income by category and month
get.description: The mirror of `GET /reports/spending`: categories of kind `income`, plus the uncategorised bucket for a month it was net positive.

get.summary: Income → category → top merchants (+ other)
get.description: One currency at a time (decision D4: no cross-currency conversion). Defaults to whichever currency has the most activity in the window.

get.summary: One budget period: assigned vs. activity, per line
get.description: A re-read of `@ctx/budgeting`'s own `getPeriod`, never a second computation of the envelope math. Pass `periodId` directly, or `budgetId` for its most recent period.

get.summary: Every table this user owns, as a versioned JSONL bundle
get.description: Needs a step-up assertion. A manifest line (contract version, per-stream row count and sha256, `created_at`, app version) followed by every row, in dependency order. `?encrypt=true` pipes the bundle through `age` to the backup recipient (docker/backup's own recipients file) and returns ciphertext instead; a 503 names why if `age` or the recipients file is unavailable rather than silently returning plaintext.

post.summary: Load a bundle into a clean instance
post.description: Needs a step-up assertion. Refused (409) unless this instance has no user data yet — import restores a whole database, it does not merge into one. Every stream's hash is verified against the manifest before anything is written; a mismatch anywhere refuses the whole bundle. Loads in one transaction, in dependency order, then re-runs `@ctx/ledger`'s own projection for every transaction rather than trusting the exported `effective_*` columns (decision D11). Body is the plaintext bundle `GET /export` produces; an `?encrypt=true` export must be decrypted with the `age` identity file before it is posted here — this application never holds that key (decision D24).

get.summary: Every user-scoped table is either exported or named exempt
get.description: The dispatch's own exit test, exposed as a route so the gate's independent reviewer can re-run it against the booted stack without a database console. Computed from `information_schema`, never a hand list (see `reports/export/registry.ts`).

get.summary: Today's budget period, with every envelope line
get.description: Lazily creates the WP 2.1 §6 default budget and opens the containing period if neither exists yet — the same 'opened by whoever first needs it' rule `apps/api/src/modules.ts` documents for `module.budgeting`.

get.summary: Every period of this budget, oldest first — the period picker

post.description: Upsert on `(periodId, categoryId)`, matching `@ctx/budgeting`'s own `upsertLine` (see this file's module comment: not on the context's public surface, re-implemented here against its published `./schema`).

The open questions: streams nobody has confirmed or rejected yet

The forward cash-flow forecast — a 30-day band by default

post.summary: Accept, dismiss, snooze or reopen an insight
post.description: A dismissal starts the 30/90/permanent cooldown ladder — the third dismissal of the same finding suppresses it permanently (`@ctx/insights`'s `policy/cooldown.ts`). An optional `reasonCode` (07 §8.3's seven-value taxonomy, WP 5.9) drives the feedback loop: NOT_TRUE counts toward the rule's quarantine rate, ALREADY_KNOW skips to the 90-day rung, DONT_CARE turns the rule off for this holder, INTENTIONAL suppresses the entity permanently. Omitted, the three legacy preset strings in `reason` are still matched by exact text.

post.description: Reaches the destination for real, through the egress policy, and reports what happened — never throws for a refusal (`{result: {ok: false, message}}` for a disallowed host, a connection failure, or a bad credential); a 404 is reserved for a channel id that does not exist at all.

delete.description: Needs a step-up assertion, the same policy as creating one. Idempotent: deleting a channel that is not (or no longer) this user’s own returns `deleted: false`, not a 404.

The delivery-attempt history for one queued notification

get.summary: Every position, aggregated by ticker across accounts
get.description: One row per security, summed over every account that holds it. `unclassifiedPct` and each row’s `stale` are fields, not inferences: 07 §4.3 makes the first normative and 07 §6.1 makes the second a statement about the clock at read time. `unresolved` (C-8, G3-11; WP 10.4) lists positions the resolver could not identify, one row per account and position, with the provider’s name and ticker, the quantity, the institution’s own value and the reasons in plain words. They are never valued, and each is also named in `excluded` (`security_unresolved`).

get.summary: The positions in one account, with their lots and basis provenance
get.description: Per-position lots with their ages, basis source, and an `unavailable` unrealized gain where the basis is unknown — 04 §5.5’s rule, carried onto the wire rather than computed from a zero. `unresolved` (C-8, G3-11; WP 10.4) is this account’s positions the resolver could not identify — never valued, and each also named in `excluded` (`security_unresolved`).

get.summary: Allocation by asset class, region and sector, with % unclassified
get.description: Fund-level only (no synthetic look-through), cash in the denominator, and `unclassifiedPct` on every dimension — present even when zero, because 07 §4.3 makes a drift claim beside a large unclassified share noise.

get.summary: Drift against a target allocation, on the absolute 5-point band
get.description: Targets are supplied as `?target=US_EQUITY:0.6`. **With no targets the response suppresses rather than invents** (07 §8 Q9): `targetsSet` is `false`, `rows` is empty, and `unclassifiedPct` is still returned. There is no `allocation_targets` table in Phase 3 — see wp3.9-routes.md §8.

get.summary: Time-weighted return, money-weighted return and dollar gain — in three shapes
get.description: 07 §4.2: never a TWR beside a dollar gain, never a benchmarked MWR. The three answers occupy three disjoint objects under three keys, so no object in this payload expresses the forbidden pairing. WP 10.3: `account` or `management` (never both — 400) restricts the valuations and the flows to that scope; `summary` is the period’s dollar picture (value, net contributions, income, fees), a fourth disjoint object with every exclusion named.

parameters.name: account
parameters.description: One account. Mutually exclusive with management.

parameters.name: management
parameters.description: Every account the holder classified so (account overrides), or `unclassified`.

get.summary: Performance per management class: advisor, robo-advisor, self-directed
get.description: One row per management class the holder has at least one investment account in, plus `unclassified` when an account has none (WP 10.3). Each row is the scoped `/investments/performance` answer: the same three disjoint objects (TWR, MWR, dollar gain) and the period summary, never merged. Only the TWR is comparable across rows (07 §4.2: it removes the effect of when money arrived); an MWR is the holder’s own rate and is never benchmarked.

put.summary: Elect the cost-basis method for one account and security
put.description: Needs a step-up assertion: `AVERAGE_COST` is sticky by database trigger (`basis_method_elections_average_cost_is_sticky`) and is a tax election the user cannot take back. **`AVERAGE_COST` is refused for anything that is not a mutual fund** — the engine does not know a security’s type, by design (wp3.2-lots.md §12 item 5), so the check belongs here, where it does.

get.summary: Investment activity: buys, sells, dividends, contributions, fees
get.description: Every investment movement in the window, newest first, with the kind the performance route classifies it as (`classifyActivity`): a contribution here is exactly an external flow there. `from`/`to` are inclusive and default to the last twelve months. Keyset pagination: pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor`. `accounts[].activitySync` distinguishes an account whose activity has not been synced yet from one that has none (WP 10.3).

total.description: Rows matching the filters in the window, across every page.

get.summary: One security: the derived facts, the user’s overlay, and the resolution
get.description: Three blocks rather than one merged object, because "what the provider said" and "what I corrected" are different questions and a screen that offered to edit the merged value could not tell the user which half they were changing.

patch.summary: Set or clear the user’s overlay on one security (04 §3.2)
patch.description: A value sets **and locks** the field; `null` clears **and unlocks** it; an absent field is untouched. `lockedFields` is not accepted from the client — a stored value that is not locked is a setting that silently does nothing. A session is enough: this writes no credential and is reversible in one call.

get.summary: The best price for one security on one date, and which rung answered
get.description: The ladder’s answer plus the raw observations behind it. `staleness` is a field: 07 §6.1’s 24-hour rule is a statement about the clock at read time, and a client deriving it from `observedAt` would derive it against a different clock.

put.summary: Write the rung-1 user price override for one security and date
put.description: Needs a step-up assertion: this is rung 1 of 07 §6.1’s ladder and outranks every provider, so it silently restates what the portfolio is worth. `close` is a decimal string — never a JSON number (D3). The write is an upsert on `(user, security, date, source, currency)`, so correcting a typo produces one row rather than two the ladder then has to choose between.

get.summary: Net worth per day over a window, gapless, with the seal on every row
get.description: One row per calendar day between `from` and `to`, from the migration’s own spine function — a day with no data comes back with `null` totals rather than being absent, because "we did not know" and "it was zero" are different facts. `sealed`, `revision`, `source` and `stalePrice` are fields: a chart cannot infer any of them. `lastSnapshotFailure` (C-9, G3-12) is non-null exactly when the most recent nightly snapshot attempt failed on a missing FX rate — 08 §6.6’s manual-entry affordance is `POST /net-worth/fx-rates`.

post.summary: 08 §6.6’s manual-entry affordance: enter an FX rate the scheduled job could not fetch
post.description: Writes `fx_rates` with `source: "user_override"` — already ranked ahead of any provider on the same date by `drizzleFxStore`’s own read order (a rate the user typed in meant it; a later provider fetch for the same day must not silently overwrite it). Needs a fresh session for the reason `POST /net-worth/corrections` does: the very next snapshot retry can use this rate to recompute a day whose total the user will see change.

rate.description: A positive decimal string, e.g. "1.0842". Never a JSON number (D3).

post.summary: Recompute one closed day and write the result as a new revision
post.description: Needs a step-up assertion. The sealed row is **never written to**: `correctDay` inserts the next revision carrying `supersedes_id` and a mandatory `correction_reason`, so the app can still answer "what did we show on the 14th?" after the 14th has been corrected. A missing FX rate is a 409 naming the pair, never a conversion at par (D4).

get.summary: Source priority, key presence, budgets and the licence obligations
get.description: Key **presence** only — there is no field in this response that could carry a key value, and the exit test plants a synthetic key and asserts its bytes appear nowhere. `attribution` carries the exact licence string and its quoted clause, because a UI cannot render an obligation it was never told about (01 §4.3).

put.summary: Reorder the price-source ladder for one security kind
put.description: Needs a step-up assertion: this decides which provider’s number becomes the price of everything the user owns. Rung numbers are **computed**, not accepted — `user_override` is pinned to 1 and `last_known` to 99 by CHECK constraints, and a client that could choose them could disable the one rung a human controls.

post.summary: One guarded live call to a provider, to prove a key works
post.description: Needs a step-up assertion — this is the only route in this work package that leaves the machine. It goes through the **existing** `PriceSource`, so it inherits WP 2.4’s egress allow-list, the literal-IP and private-address refusals, the timeout and the rate budget, and it spends against that budget like any other call. With no key configured it answers `skipped_no_key` and makes no request at all. No response field can carry a key value, and any provider error text is run through `redactedMessageOf` before it is returned.

post.summary: Run the price refresh for the caller now
post.description: Runs the nightly price refresh (`integrations.price_refresh`) for the caller immediately: every security with a non-zero position, routed by kind to the provider that prices it (Tiingo for equities, ETFs and funds; CoinGecko for crypto), plus FX for every non-USD position currency through FRED. Spends against the same per-provider budgets as the schedule. At most one run per holder per ten minutes: 409 `market_data.refresh_too_soon` with `Retry-After` and the instant in the detail. The response names every security that was not priced and why.

get.summary: Where a market-data key comes from, without the key
get.description: Whether a key for this provider is in force, and whether it is the operator's secret file (read-only here), this holder’s stored key, or neither — and for OpenFIGI, whether the anonymous tier is in use. Carries the last four characters of a stored key and its dates. The key is never returned (WP 10.4).

put.summary: Store (or replace) this holder’s key for one market-data provider
put.description: Needs a step-up assertion (D21). Checks the key with the provider (one cheap authenticated call through the existing adapter) before sealing it under the KEK. 409 when the operator's secret file supplies this provider's key; 409 `market_data.provider_narrowed_out` when MARKET_DATA_ALLOWED_HOSTS excludes the host; 422 when the provider refuses the key; 502 when it cannot be reached. Nothing is stored unless the provider accepted the key. The response is the GET shape; the key is never returned.

key.description: The API key. Validated with the provider, sealed, and never echoed back.

delete.summary: Remove this holder’s stored key for one market-data provider
delete.description: Needs a step-up assertion (D21). Deletes the sealed row and retires its key. Revokes nothing at the provider. Leaves an operator's secret file untouched. Idempotent. Returns the GET shape.

get.summary: Every goal of the caller, oldest first

post.summary: Create a goal
post.description: A target date already in the past, or a funding account that does not exist or is closed, is a 422 domain refusal — never clamped to today and never dropped from the list (`packages/contexts/planning/src/goals.ts`’s own header).

get.summary: One goal

patch.description: Each field present is re-validated by the same rule creation uses.

delete.summary: Delete a goal (its contribution plans and earmarks go with it, by cascade)

get.summary: One goal's contribution plans

post.summary: Add a contribution plan to a goal
post.description: The amount must be in the goal’s own currency (a mismatch is a 409 domain refusal, never a silent conversion); `escalationPct` is a decimal string and a number is refused rather than converted (D3).

delete.description: Two scoping predicates, both load-bearing and genuinely independent: (1) the goal named in the URL must be the caller’s — enforced by `listContributions`’s own `getGoal` call, so a stray `goalId` refuses before this route reads a single contribution row; (2) the contribution named in the URL must actually belong to *that* goal, not merely to the caller — a caller who owns both the named goal and the named contribution, but under *different* goals, is refused by the second check even though the first is satisfied. (An earlier draft of this route also called `getGoal` directly before this line, as a distinct "predicate 1" — removed once the sabotage matrix showed it was never independently load-bearing: dropping it left the route exactly as secure, because `listContributions` already re-derives the same fact. Recorded in `docs/evidence/phase-4/wp4.8-routes.md` as the finding it is, in the spirit of WP 3.9’s S1 — a predicate that "passes when dropped" is telling you something, and the answer here was "this check was redundant", not "insecure".)

get.summary: The consistency-penalty questionnaire's instrument, and the caller's current score
get.description: The score is read-only here: it is derived from the answers and cannot be set directly (`PUT /risk-profile` is the only way to move it, and it always answers the whole questionnaire again).

put.summary: Answer the questionnaire; derive, band and store a new score
put.description: When the two framings of a disposition disagree, the score moves to the more conservative one, never to the mean; the `explanation` array is the sentence the holder sees, one per disposition and then the total. Declining `income` leaves `taxBracketBand: null` rather than inventing one; the income itself never reaches the stored row (08 §4.2).

get.summary: The baseline (if stated) first, then its forks oldest first

post.summary: State (or restate) the baseline, or fork it
post.description: A `"baseline"` body upserts the one baseline scenario: a second call replaces the profile and keeps the id and seed, so every fork and every stored run still points at it. A `"fork"` body stores only the levers that differ from the baseline — a fork that restates every lever is refused (`planning.scenario_levers_empty`, 422).

post.summary: Serve a scenario’s projection from the cache, or run it
post.description: An identical request (same assumptions, seed, engine version and input) is served from `projection_runs` without running the engine again. `method` defaults to `monte_carlo` when a Monte Carlo engine is bound in this process, `deterministic` otherwise; the response says which ran. `successProbability` is a decimal string, never a JSON number.

acceptAccountChanges.description: WP 9.2. After the holder changes an account’s tax treatment, role or valuation, the stored run comes back `stale` and nothing is computed. `true` says they know and asks for a new run from the current settings.

get.summary: A stored run, exactly as stored, with its staleness named
get.description: Never recomputes. A run whose assumptions version this build does not hold as the current file reads back `assumptions_version_retired` — whether the version is not held at all, or (since the guardrail-rate move retained its predecessor) is held only as a frozen, resolvable-but-superseded file. A run whose version is itself the current file, but whose current assumptions differ from the run’s, reads back `assumptions_changed`.

post.summary: The additional monthly contribution that closes a gap by a target date
post.description: A gap no contribution can close returns `"unreachable"` with the binding constraint — never a number that implies a solution. Name a `goalId` to solve for that goal’s own target and date, or state `objective` directly for an arbitrary date/amount or for "sustain the plan to its end".

get.summary: The caller's life events, in date order

post.summary: Add a dated, signed life event to the plan timeline
post.description: The sign is the direction: an inheritance or windfall must be positive, a home purchase, college or sabbatical must be negative — a mismatch is a 422 refusal, never a silently flipped sign.

patch.summary: Move a life event on the timeline, or restate its name or amount
patch.description: Not in the dispatch’s literal route list (`GET/POST/DELETE /plan/life-events`), added because `@ctx/planning`’s `updateLifeEvent` exists for exactly this — WP 4.10’s own dispatch text names "draggable life events" as a WP 4.8 contract dependency, and there is no way to drag one without a route that moves it. Recorded as an addition, not hidden as an implicit part of the literal list (`docs/evidence/phase-4/wp4.8-routes.md`).

get.summary: Two scenarios, run under common random numbers, and their deltas
get.description: Both runs use the baseline’s seed — a fork has none of its own (0022) — so the comparison isolates the levers’ effect from Monte Carlo noise by construction, not by the caller remembering to pass the same seed twice.

get.summary: The cited assumptions file, resolved against the caller's overrides
get.description: Every number in the file lives in a cited node — `kind`, `value`, `source`, `asOf` and, where present, `note`/`attribution` — and this response carries the file whole, not a subset. An overridden path keeps the shape: its `source` reads "Your override (the default is …)" and its `asOf` is the day it was set.

put.summary: Replace the caller's overrides (full desired-value semantics)
put.description: Only the seventeen capital-market paths in `overridablePaths` may be overridden; an unknown path or a non-decimal value is a 422. A value that equals the current default is dropped — an override never pins a stale default — and `{}` clears every override back to the file's own numbers.

get.summary: Every scope permitted for this advisor, sensitivity order, with grant status
get.description: 08 §4.2’s catalogue, filtered to what this advisor’s execution mode may ever hold (`externalAllowed`) — a scope an `external` advisor could never be granted is not listed as a choice at all, rather than listed and then refused.

put.summary: Replace the caller’s standing scope grants for one advisor
put.description: Needs a fresh session (D21): a standing grant of `holdings.detail` or similar is credential-access-class consent. Full desired-set semantics — a scope present in the body and not currently granted is granted; a scope currently granted and absent from the body is revoked. A scope outside the published v1 enum is a 400 before this handler runs; one published but not permitted for this advisor’s kind is a 422 named here, before `grantScopes` is called.

get.summary: The consent history for one advisor: every grant, revoke and re-grant, newest first
get.description: O-9. Append-only: a re-grant is a new row beside the revoke it follows, never a rewrite of either. Each row carries the step-up session that authorised it. Bounded to the 200 most recent events.

get.summary: The most recently published Weekly Advisory Brief
get.description: Served exactly as stored (05 §3 WP 5.10) — no ranking, no retirement-effect recomputation. 404 `insights.brief_not_found` when no Brief has ever been published.

get.summary: One week’s published Weekly Advisory Brief, by its ISO week
The holder’s financial health score, with its six-component breakdown
get.description: The most recently computed week (05 §3 WP 5.8), served exactly as stored — no recomputation on read, the same rule the Brief above follows. Six named components, each with value, band, weight, score and direction of travel against the previous stored week; a component with no data is named in `excluded`, never scored as zero (09 ADV-7). 404 `insights.health_score_not_computed` when no score has ever been computed for this holder.

get.summary: The most recent runs of one advisor, newest first
The run inspector: one run, with its retained payload re-verified
get.description: `payload.digestVerified` is recomputed server-side from the retained bytes against `input_digest`, never trusted from storage — see this file’s header.

post.summary: Kill level 4: ask one in-flight run to stop
post.description: Needs a fresh session. The run watcher notices within about a second and closes `cancelled` with `cancel_reason = run_cancelled`; nothing is written after the kill. 409 `insights.run_not_in_flight` when the run has already finished.

get.summary: The exact payload a run of this advisor would send now — invokes nothing
get.description: Sends nothing to any model (see this file’s header). For a `local_model` advisor whose prompt bytes cannot be shown on this process, `prompt` is `null` and `promptTemplateHash` still names the template — see "Needs the orchestrator" in this WP's evidence.

post.summary: Approve the payload shape a preview returned
post.description: Needs a fresh session. Carries the `queryShape` the preview returned; refuses 409 `insights.payload_shape_changed` if the advisor’s shape has changed since — a scope granted, a version bumped or a template edited. The approval is for exactly what was shown, never for "whatever this advisor sends next".

get.summary: Kill switch 2, as it stands: the kind flag, the model configuration and both together
get.description: What the settings screen shows instead of the last `PUT`: `enabled` is the flag the holder controls, `configured` is whether this deployment has a model configured for the kind (`LOCAL_MODEL_PIN_*` on the api, or the full `LOCAL_MODEL_*` set), and `effective` is both. Only a kind with a declared flag has a state; 404 `insights.kind_flag_not_found` otherwise, exactly as the `PUT`.

put.summary: Kill switch 2: turn every advisor of one kind on or off
put.description: Needs a fresh session — the same class of act as `POST /advisors/{id}/enabled` (D21). Only a kind with a declared flag can be switched here; today that is `local_model` (`advisors.kind.local_model`, off by default).

get.summary: Kill switch 1, as it stands: the operator setting, the holder’s flag and both together
get.description: `operator.advisorsEnabled` is `ADVISORS_ENABLED` (static per process; the operator changes it with a restart). `user.enabled` is `module.insights`, which the holder flips with `PUT /advisors/module/enabled` (G5-14: until now it was a line of SQL).

put.summary: Kill switch 1, the holder’s half: turn the insights module on or off
put.description: Writes `module.insights`. Needs a fresh session — the same class of act as the kind switch and `POST /advisors/{id}/enabled` (D21). Off stops every advisor of every kind within about a second, a run in flight included (WP 5.1). Returns the state as it now stands, the operator half included.

get.summary: Every registered advisor's health: firings, dismissals by reason, NOT_TRUE rate
Backup and restore-drill status (D24, CF-17)
get.description: Install-wide, not account-holder data: the newest successful backup’s age and the newest restore drill’s verdict and age. `backupOverdue` turns true past the nightly cadence’s staleness window (or with no successful backup at all); `drillOverdue` turns true past 35 days since the last drill (or with no drill at all).

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Passkeys, TOTP fallback, recovery codes, sessions and step-up. Tokens travel in `__Host-` cookies and never in a response body.

tags.name: accounts
tags.description: Accounts, their latest balances, and net worth. Every balance says when.

tags.name: transactions
tags.description: The feed, the overlay, splits, transfers and the CSV export. Pagination is keyset: pass `nextCursor` back verbatim.

tags.name: connections
tags.description: Providers, the link and reconnect flows, sync history, and the server-sent event streams that carry sync progress.

tags.name: categories
tags.description: The chart of categories this user may assign to. Per user (decision D6), seeded from the shipped taxonomy at boot, and editable by the user thereafter — so the list is read from the table, never from the constant.

tags.name: rules
tags.description: The categorisation rule language, as CRUD, plus preview/apply and "always categorise like this transaction". A session is enough — see rules.ts's module comment for why this file does not need a step-up assertion.

tags.name: reports
tags.description: Spending, income, the Sankey and budget-vs-actual — pure aggregation over the contexts' own read models. Transfers excluded and refunds netted, reusing `@ctx/budgeting`'s rule rather than re-deriving it.

tags.name: export
tags.description: The full-database bundle: export as a versioned, hash-checked JSONL stream, and import into a clean instance. Both need a step-up assertion.

tags.name: budgets
tags.description: The envelope budget: periods, lines, assignments and rolls. A session is enough — every write here edits the user's own plan, never a credential.

tags.name: recurring
tags.description: Subscriptions and bills: the candidate queue, confirmed streams, the forecast and safe-to-spend. A session is enough.

tags.name: insights
tags.description: The advisory feed and the advisor registry: review an insight, and the three kill switches. Turning an advisor on/off or triggering a run needs a step-up assertion.

tags.name: notifications
tags.description: Channels, rules and the delivery outbox. Attaching or destroying a channel needs a step-up assertion, the same policy as a connection's credential.

tags.name: investments
tags.description: Holdings aggregated across accounts, per-account lots and basis provenance, allocation, drift, performance, securities and prices. `unclassifiedPct` and `stale` are always fields, never inferences; a time-weighted return, a money-weighted return and a dollar gain never share an object (07 §4.2). A session is enough to read and to set an overlay; the rung-1 price override and the sticky basis-method election need a step-up assertion.

tags.name: planning
tags.description: Net worth over time. The series is gapless and a day with no data is `null`, not zero; sealed days are labelled as such. A correction never rewrites a sealed row — it writes the next revision with its reason — and needs a step-up assertion.

tags.name: market-data
tags.description: Price-source priority, provider key **presence** (never a key value), rate budgets, the licence obligations that bind on any surface showing these numbers, and a guarded test fetch. Both writes need a step-up assertion.
